findings.claim: When `root` normalizes to the filesystem root ("/"), the returned relative dist dir loses its leading separator, unlike every other root value.
findings.rationale: `normalizedRoot.length` is used for the slice instead of `rootPrefix.length`, deliberately preserving the leading '/' (root '/a' + dist '/a/dist' -> '/dist'). But for normalizedRoot === '/', length is 1 and the slice removes the separator, yielding 'dist' instead of '/dist'. This inconsistency will surprise any caller that concatenates or path-joins the result. High confidence this is an inconsistency; impact depends on the (not-shown) call site.

findings.claim: `startsWith` is case- and drive-letter-sensitive, so a root that actually contains distDir can silently return "" on Windows or case-insensitive macOS volumes.
findings.rationale: Paths like 'C:/proj' vs 'c:/proj', or differing case on a case-insensitive APFS/HFS+ volume, are the same directory but fail the exact string prefix test, producing the 'not contained' sentinel. Moderate confidence this matters in practice for Vitest's Windows support.

findings.claim: The empty-string return value conflates three distinct cases: distDir outside root, root === distDir, and a failed prefix match.
findings.rationale: When `root` equals `distDir`, `rootPrefix` gains a trailing slash so `startsWith` is false and '' is returned, the same as the genuinely-outside-root case. Callers cannot distinguish 'no relative path' from 'dist dir is the root itself'. Returning null/undefined for the not-contained case would be unambiguous. Medium confidence this causes a real bug without seeing the consumer.

findings.claim: The trailing-slash regex, the `${normalizedRoot}/` prefix, and the `=== '/'` check all assume `normalize` emits POSIX separators.
findings.rationale: If `normalize` is Node's `path.normalize` rather than pathe's, on Windows it emits backslashes and none of this logic works (regex won't strip 'C:\\', prefix mixes separators, startsWith fails). Low-to-medium confidence since Vitest usually imports from pathe, but the import is outside the shown hunk and worth verifying.
